findings.where: Brief 2.3 :275-277 (option A: a strictly newer command runs whenever it arrives, up to 8 per tick); 2.4 :298-302 (kind 1 is only an upper bound against the room's tick; kind 2 compares only with the newest accepted command, and a fresh slot has none); 2.6 :368-369; Q8 :1149-1151; Q11 (v) :1197-1198; section 12 item 6 :1361-1365. Code: room/src/input.rs:23, :107-113 (option B's only lower anchor is `ran_through`; option A gets none); sim/src/world.rs:1030 and :1333-1345, :1389-1395 (each command run is one tick of movement, weapon clock and reload); ADR 0001:231-233.
findings.summary: Under option A nothing ties a command's stamp to the room's tick from below. Exploit: a client joins and stamps its first command T-2^31+1 (or T-100,000). That passes kind 1 (not ahead) and kind 2 (no reference on a fresh slot). It then sends 2 datagrams of 8 commands per tick, each stamp one higher than the last. Every one passes kinds 1 and 2, so the room runs 8 a tick. That is 8x movement, fire rate and reload speed for as long as the bank lasts (up to 2^31 commands). A cheater who already joined honestly gets the same effect by sending nothing for 60 s and then 8 a tick for about 257 ticks. ADR 0001:231-233's claim (never more commands than the server's ticks plus the lead bound) holds only from an anchored first stamp. -21's cheats never build such a bank: the fast clock starts at newest + lead (Q11 (v) (b)) and the lag switch holds only 200 ms. So the judged -21 fast-clock and lag-switch checks would pass on a build with this hole. The lead bound's 'at most 12 more commands per 60 s' in Q8 and the LEAD-BOUND draft for Mustafa assume the anchor too. My night SA-1 fix offered a [-W, bound] window as one route; rev 2 and rev 3 took only the sort half.
findings.fix: (1) Add a join anchor under both options: on a fresh slot, kind 2's reference is the room's tick at join, so a command stamped at or before it is refused as kind 2. Add f13 (iii): a fresh slot whose first stamp is T-1,000, and one at T-2^31+1, is refused as kind 2 and nothing runs. This also removes SA-1's triple without relying on the sort. (2) Add a new U4F-Q18 for option A's past window. (a) recommended: a command stamped more than W = CMD_CATCHUP ticks (8, carry 27's constant, no new rate constant) before the tick being run is dropped and counted `late` (not forged) and never runs. The bank is then at most 8 commands. Plan :439-441's 8 recovered commands after a burst fit, and the catch-up kind's 16 commands fit inside W + bound. (b) No window: the idle bank is written up as option A's speed-hack exposure for OQ-0001-6, and ADR 0001:231-233 is read as 'from join' (readings PR). (3) Tests and runs: f19 gains an option-A idle-then-fast case (idle N ticks, then 8 a tick: at most W extra commands run). Add a reported short run p20 (fast clock, option A, idle before each episode; excess at most W, reported, not judged; judging it would be a bar for him under 5.6). (4) Before B3 goes to him, Q8's allowances and section 12 item 6's LEAD-BOUND text say 'under option A: the bound plus W', or name the open bank under (b). (5) Section 7 item 2 reports the anchor and W as built. With (1) and (2a) every slot's ticks lie within 2^31, so Q17 (b) also becomes safe; (a), the total key, stays the recommendation.

findings.where: Brief 2.6 :357-361 (the forger forges the command it stores, so every redundant copy carries the forgery); 2.12 :551-552; Q13 (b) :1219-1220 ('its sequence index skipped'); 2.13 :572 ('a sequence skip'). Code: proto/src/input.rs:19-21 and encoder :155-159 (a repeat's sequence is its newer neighbour's minus one; its tick step must be 0 to 255); client/src/lib.rs:466-469 (an Input that fails to encode is not sent at all).
findings.summary: Several forgeries and twins the brief describes cannot be encoded, or are counted under the wrong kind. (i) Kind 1: a stored far-ahead copy riding behind a newer honest command needs a negative tick step, so the encoder returns OutOfRange and the forger's datagrams stop going out. (ii) Kind 3: if the forgery is stored, its first copy is a new sequence with valid content, which runs. Kind 3 is then never refused, and unrejected reads 1,000 on a correct build. (iii) The twin's 'sequence skip' leaves a gap in the unacknowledged list. The encoder returns NotCanonical, and the twin endpoint sends no Input until the gap leaves its window, so f16 fails on a correct build. (iv) Under Q13 (b), later honest copies of a refused sequence differ from the kept content. They are counted as kind 3 on every kind 1, 2, 4, 5 or 6 forger, against 2.5's '0 outside its kind' and f15. My own night SA-3 fix proposed 'every copy' without checking the codec.
findings.fix: In 2.6 and 2.12, per kind: kinds 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 forge only the copy that carries the command as the newest, and the endpoint keeps the honest command. The repeat filter treats every later copy of a refused sequence as a repeat (uncounted, it can never run), whatever its content. Kind 3 forges the content of one redundant copy of a sequence the room has accepted (P0: received in order). The twin's script makes no command at that step, so its sequences stay consecutive; the state hash excludes command bookkeeping (sim/src/world.rs:1922-1925). The catch-up twin is built the same way. Replace 2.13's 'a sequence skip' and Q13 (b)'s wording to match. f15 asserts that every forged and twin datagram encodes (no EncodeError) under both options; f16 stays before the judged sets.

findings.where: Brief 2.4, kind 4 row :321 ('x² + y² ≤ 127², integers'); sim/src/seam.rs:35 (move_xy is [i8; 2]); spikes/netcode-proof/Cargo.toml:116-120 (release overflow checks are on for npt-sim and npt-proto only).
findings.summary: The brief does not say how wide kind 4's arithmetic is. Squaring a forged [-128, -128] move in i8 or i16 overflows. A debug or test build panics on network input; a release room build wraps to a negative sum and accepts the command.
findings.fix: 2.4's kind 4 row: widen x and y to i32 before squaring, and never call abs() on a wire value. f10's kind 4 case adds [-128, -128] and [-128, 0], both refused.

findings.summary: The kept window is defined by distance from the newest sequence. Nothing says what happens to a sequence inside K whose command was never received, so the window holds no entry for it. Example: an overtaken datagram carries the one sequence the overtaking datagram lacked. If 'content that differs' is read as kind 3, an honest copy is counted as forged.
findings.fix: 2.4 item 2: a sequence with no kept entry is dropped and counted under the outside-window counter (`seq_outside_window`, not forged), never as kind 3. f12 gains case (v) for it.

findings.where: Brief section 4 :610-724; section 11 D3 :1287; U4F-Q4 (a) :1092-1093; U4F-Q6 (b) :1116-1118. Code: server/src/pump.rs:461-466 and client/src/lib.rs:473-478 (Pong travels both ways); lab/src/scenario.rs:115-125 (seeded tokens).

Q6 (b): the room ignores, or refuses as an unknown field, the sub-tick field in a client's Pong, with a negative case among its tests (+1).

findings.where: Brief 2.1 ping row :250 ('ping_limited 0 on a clean run'); 2.6 fast-clock row :368; server/src/pump.rs:458-472 (10 pings a second).
findings.summary: The client pings only at its steps. A 1.5x host clock therefore pings 1.5 times as often: 15 a second at D4's one ping every 3 steps, over the room's limit of 10. The cheat client's `ping_limited` count rises above 0 and its ClockSync gets fewer samples. That is expected behaviour, but it will be read against the brief's 'ping_limited 0' line.
findings.fix: 2.6's fast-clock row states the cheat's expected `ping_limited` (reported, not a failure), or sets a ping period of at most two-thirds of the limit so a 1.5x clock stays inside it.

findings.summary: Under option A the catch-up cap refuses at the tick's run, so the room's per-slot list of commands arrived for the coming tick is bounded only by the pump's bucket (8 datagrams, then 2 a tick, of up to 8 commands each), not by the room itself.
findings.fix: Under option A the room refuses a new command on arrival once 8 are held for the coming tick, counted as kind 10, so its list never exceeds CMD_CATCHUP whatever the pump does. Q9 (a)'s flood test asserts it.

summary:
Rev 3 of the U4f builder brief fails the hostile-input check: one High, two Medium and five Low findings. The High needs a revision before the advisor sees the brief.

**My night findings SA-1 to SA-17.** The three Highs:
- SA-2 (the counting order, the same finding as the test-engineer's TE-1) is fixed as a question to the advisor (U4F-Q9, recommendation (a)), and rev 3 keeps the fix.
- SA-1 (the sort with no total order, which can panic and stop the room for all clients): the sort half is fixed as a question (U4F-Q17 recommends the total key; tests f8 and f9, run item D14). The other half of my night fix, a window of accepted stamps around the room's tick, was not taken. That gap is the new High below. A small wording slip: the total key equals today's order only for ticks less than 2^31 apart from each other, not for every tick within 2^31 of the tick being run.
- SA-3 (a refused command is still acknowledged, so it is never resent) stays open as a question (U4F-Q13). The forgery and twin construction it now relies on clashes with the Input encoding (SA3-2).

SA-4, SA-8, SA-10 and SA-12 to SA-17 are fixed and still fixed. SA-5, SA-6, SA-7, SA-9 and SA-11 are fixed as questions; SA-9's window has one undefined case (SA3-4).

**New findings.**
- **SA3-1 (High): option A has no lower bound on a command's stamp.** A fresh slot's first stamp can be 2^31 ticks in the past, and a client that sends nothing for a while builds up the same credit. Either way the client then runs 8 commands a tick for as long as the credit lasts. That is 8x movement, fire rate and reload, because each command run is one tick for the soldier (sim/src/world.rs:1030, :1389-1395). The -21 cheats never build that credit, so the judged fast-clock and lag-switch checks would pass on a build with the hole. The lead-bound allowance that goes to Mustafa for his yes (LEAD-BOUND) assumes the bound exists. Fix: anchor kind 2 at the join tick, plus a new question on a past window of 8 ticks under option A.
- **SA3-2 (Medium):** some forgeries and twins as described cannot be encoded, or get counted under the wrong kind.
- **SA3-5 (Medium):** the brief plans to pack U4f's own run-log folders, which the advisor's R4 ('pack only by brief 8.1's rules') and Mustafa's PACK-READ (a) ('one or two closed, older log folders') do not cover.
- **Lows:** SA3-3 (the move-length check's integer width), SA3-4 (a sequence the window has no entry for), SA3-6 (no stated network rule, D3's command form, the log key must never be the token, the client-sent side of the proposed Pong field), SA3-7 (the 1.5x client's pings exceed the ping limit), SA3-8 (option A's waiting list is bounded only by the server's rate limit, not by the room).

**Hostile-input coverage.**

No forged kind leads to a kick. The counters are u64 and grow by at most 8 per message, so they cannot overflow; no check loops over client-sized data beyond 16, 8 or the event cap.
